method: ENTIRELY from ONE AMH page, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED. No passage reproduced, no source_text stored, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable and every statement must be verified by a person against a current subscription. ⚠️ THE PAGE NAMES DRUGS AND COURSE LENGTHS BUT NO mg DOSE. Its comparative table gives pregnancy, breastfeeding, paediatric and adverse-effect columns, which are recorded here. The individual benzimidazole and other anthelmintic monographs were NOT retrieved.

claims.claim: ⚠️ AUSTRALIA IS FREE OF MANY WORM (HELMINTH) INFECTIONS, BUT THREADWORM (Enterobius vermicularis) INFECTION IS COMMON THROUGHOUT. HOOKWORMS (Ancylostoma duodenale, Necator americanus), THE COMMON ROUNDWORM (Ascaris lumbricoides), THE WHIPWORM (Trichuris trichiura) AND Strongyloides stercoralis ARE NOT UNCOMMON IN NORTHERN AUSTRALIA. HYDATID (Echinococcus granulosus) DISEASE IS OCCASIONALLY SEEN, PARTICULARLY IN RESIDENTS AND FORMER RESIDENTS OF FARMING COMMUNITIES. A traveller may acquire these or other infections, eg SCHISTOSOMIASIS, overseas
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Worm infections' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/anthelmintics/worm-infections, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ WHETHER WORMS CAUSE DISEASE DEPENDS PARTICULARLY ON THE INTENSITY OF INFECTION -- with most intestinal worms, DISEASE DEVELOPS ONLY IF THE WORM BURDEN IS SUFFICIENTLY HIGH. In some infections, PARTICULARLY HYDATIDS, THE LOCATION OF THE WORM IS IMPORTANT. ⚠️ WITH THE EXCEPTION OF S. STERCORALIS, WORMS CANNOT MULTIPLY IN THE HUMAN HOST and the burden depends on duration and intensity of exposure to eggs and larvae

claims.claim: STRONGYLOIDIASIS: PREFERRED TREATMENT IS A SINGLE DOSE OF IVERMECTIN; USE A 3-DAY COURSE OF ALBENDAZOLE IN PEOPLE UNABLE TO TAKE IVERMECTIN, eg CHILDREN UNDER 15 kg. ⚠️ IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PEOPLE NEED LONGER TREATMENT -- SEEK SPECIALIST ADVICE
